files.description: The rules of the repository: what the page is, its layout, the rules it follows, how it is checked, the workflow, the writing style, how it moves independently of sqzer-dev/sqzer
What the page is, how to run it, how the version of sqzer is bumped, how a browser is checked
The index of design and behaviour decisions, and which decisions taken in sqzer-dev/sqzer govern this page

The design of the page: the drop zone as the empty state, the image on the whole screen under glass panels, the target first and every package option behind Advanced, untouched controls sending nothing, the search shown as it runs, the result as size, difference and chips, errors as alerts, the privacy claim, the wordmark, the accessibility floor

The stack: React 19 and TypeScript under Vite with the Rust React Compiler, `<ViewTransition>` and `<Activity>`, the search as an XState machine with the worker as an actor, `sqzer` from npm served from the page's own origin, the Content-Security-Policy injected at build, Feature-Sliced Design, oxlint, Vitest browser mode, Playwright, the layout, the deploy and Dependabot

The components and the look: shadcn/ui on Base UI under `<CSPProvider disableStyleElements>`, Tailwind 4 as the one styling system, Geist Sans and Mono self-hosted, Radix Colors grey mapped onto shadcn's tokens, one `glass` utility with its fallbacks and contrast test, Lucide icons, the licence notices

The worker's lifetime and the layout: the worker actor is invoked by the machine's `open` state and keeps the decoded image between searches, cancelling is re-entering `open`, every message names its image, and slices are merged into `src/pages/compress/` until something is reused
The messages between the page and the worker: what the client sends, what the worker answers, and the stages a failure names
